subject: Throughput sizing follow-up — Finex performance targets
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Peterson <jonas@finexcap.com>; Aisha Rahman <aisha@finexcap.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + sizing info request — Finex performance targets

Hi Jonas / Aisha,

Thanks for the time earlier — good conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Goal: Understand Finex's latency SLOs and throughput profile so we can size a Dedicated or Hosted plan appropriately.
- Action items for Finex: send expected peak and steady-state QPS, average tokens per request, concurrency (simultaneous active requests), and whether streaming partial responses is required.
- Redwood next steps: preliminary throughput worksheet (attached), identify kernel/quantization recommendations, and propose a short sizing call if there are gaps.

Questions to help us size:
1) Typical prompt + response token count (avg and 95th).
2) Expected peak QPS (requests/sec) and sustained QPS.
3) Concurrent active sessions you need to support.
4) Are you using streaming (token-by-token) or do you need full-response buffering?
5) Acceptable P50/P95 latency targets (per-token or end-to-end).

I've attached a short worksheet (finex-throughput-worksheet.xlsx) you can fill; also attached our qualifying questions (redwood-qual-questions.pdf). If you can get that back by EOD Friday it would be great.

Thanks — I cc'd Marissa from Solutions so she can chime in on any model/quant questions.

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com

From: Jonas Peterson <jonas@finexcap.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-19T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + sizing info request — Finex performance targets

Thanks Rafael — following up with the numbers from our side (see below). Aisha is cc'd for follow-up on traffic patterns.

Quick answers:
- Typical payload: prompt ~120 tokens, expected model completion ~480 tokens; average end-to-end ~600 tokens. 95th percentile is ~1,200 tokens.
- Peak QPS: 25 requests/sec (expected at market open spikes).
- Sustained QPS (steady state): ~5 requests/sec.
- Concurrent active requests: we expect up to 20 concurrent requests during peak windows.
- Streaming: yes — we need partial result streaming for the trading UI (low-latency first-token delivery matters).
- Latency targets: P50 end-to-end < 100ms; P95 end-to-end < 250ms is ideal. We can tolerate up to 300ms P95 under heavy load but would like to avoid it.

Extra context: most requests are short chat-style queries from traders (low context), but we have a subset of batch jobs that run longer summaries (those hit the 1,200 token tail). Also we expect bursts that last 5–10 minutes (market events) rather than sustained hour-long peaks.

Let me know if you need exact percentiles over a day; Aisha can share a CSV from our traffic logs.

—Jonas
Jonas Peterson
Head of Platform, Finex Capital
jonas@finexcap.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Peterson <jonas@finexcap.com>; Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + sizing info request — Finex performance targets

Jonas — thanks for the details, that's super helpful. Quick read of the numbers and a few clarifying Qs before we lock sizing:

Initial sizing notes (very rough, assumes a 7B-class open model with quantized runtime):
- Avg request ~600 tokens at peak 25 QPS -> ~15,000 tokens/sec peak.
- If we assume ~8 tokens per GPU token/sec on quantized 7B path (conservative), that's ~1,875 effective model-token-seconds -> suggests 1-2 A100-class GPUs for peak, or 2 x L40-type instances depending on batch behavior.
- Steady-state 5 QPS -> ~3,000 tokens/sec -> comfortably handled on a single smaller instance or burstable pool.

Questions to confirm:
1) When you say streaming, do you need true server-sent streaming with early token flushes (we can support partial flushes) or is incremental chunking acceptable?
2) For the 1,200 token tail: how frequently do those occur (percent of requests)? If >5% we should size for a modest larger memory/kv-cache profile.
3) Are you planning to send batched requests from your side or one request per UI action? Batching changes throughput calculations substantially.

Next steps I propose:
- Rafael / I can put together a short sizing proposal (specific instance types, expected latency headroom, and cost estimate).
- If fine, schedule a 30-minute follow-up to review the worksheet + proposed sizing.

I'm attaching the worksheet we used and a short doc with qualifying questions — feel free to fill or send the CSV Aisha mentioned.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
